predecessors.name: Republic of China
predecessors.text: Guangdong, the base of the Guangzhou government around Canton

successors.name: Republic of China
successors.text: all of China under the Nationalist flag after 29 December 1928: the Nationalist government at Nanjing is the government of the Republic of China, whose Cliopatria row resumes in 1930

ledger.x: 1917: Sun Yat-sen sets up a rival military government at Guangzhou.
1920: Chen Jiongming invades Guangdong.
1920: the Guangdong-Guangxi War ends with Guangzhou in the hands of Sun's side.
1921: the military government becomes an 'extraordinary presidency'.
1922: Chen Jiongming drives Sun out of Guangzhou.
1923: Sun retakes Guangzhou for the third time.
1926: Guangxi's army fights as part of the Northern Expedition.
1926: the Northern Expedition takes Hunan.
1926: Jiangxi changes hands.
1926: Wuchang surrenders and Hubei is won.
1926: the KMT retakes Nanchang on 9 November and holds Jiangxi.
1926: the Jiangxi fighting ends when 'The KMT retook Nanchang on 9 November 1926'.
1926: Fujian is won without a fight.
1927: Zhejiang falls under KMT control.
1927: the Northern Expedition enters Shanghai on 22 March: 'Bai Chongxi's forces entered Shanghai on 22 March 1927.'
1927: the Northern Expedition enters Nanjing on 24 March: 'Cheng Qian entered Nanjing on 24 March 1927, with no resistance.'
1927: Chiang Kai-shek declares Nanjing the capital on 18 April, against the left-wing government at Wuhan.
1927: Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun leaves its Shaanxi base and takes Henan for the Nationalist side.
1928: the Guangxi clique holds Hubei and Hunan as well as Guangxi inside the Nationalist army.
April 1928: the Communists hold the Jinggang Mountains base on the Jiangxi-Hunan border.
ledger.cpn: Chinese Communists (Jinggangshan and Jiangxi soviet bases)

ledger.x: 1928: the NRA takes Jinan on 30 April.
1928: Yan Xishan enters Beijing.
1928: Manchuria joins the Nationalist flag.
29 December 1928: the Nationalist government absorbs the Beiyang Republic and is the government of China.
1929: the Guangxi clique's Guangxi; as below, the relation continues in republic-of-china and is ended by the Central Plains War of May 1930.
1929: the Guangxi clique's realm.
1929: Feng Yuxiang's realm; continued in republic-of-china and ended by the Central Plains War of May 1930.
1929: Yan Xishan's realm; continued in republic-of-china and ended by the Central Plains War of May 1930.
1929: Zhang Xueliang's Manchuria; continued in republic-of-china until the Japanese invasion of 1931.
1929: the Cliopatria row changes from Kuomintang to Republic of China.

wars.name: Guangdong-Guangxi War
wars.outcome: Chen Jiongming expelled the Guangxi clique from Guangzhou and Sun returned by the end of November 1920.

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: Hunan and Hubei in 1926, Jiangxi and Fujian by December 1926, Zhejiang, Shanghai and Nanjing in February-March 1927, the split of April 1927, Jinan on 30 April and Beijing on 6 June 1928, Manchuria's allegiance on 29 December 1928.

wars.name: Jinan incident
wars.outcome: The Japanese attacked Jinan on 8 May 1928, killing about 5,000 Chinese civilians; the page does not give a territorial result.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War (opening: Shanghai massacre)
wars.outcome: Begun by the Shanghai purge of 12-14 April 1927: 'On 12 April 1927, Chiang Kai-shek violently purged the communists in what was known as the Shanghai massacre.

certainty.note: The Guangzhou government's reach in Guangdong shifted with Chen Jiongming and the Guangxi clique; no boundary is on the pages.
Expedition fronts and the realms of the allied army groups are approximate; the provincial lines of the south are administrative and firm where the ledger names a province.
